div.p: In this paper, we present a kind of general application software framework for unmanned air vehicle (UAV) airborne computer based on the VxWorks real-time operating system. The detailed designs of task classification, priorities and intertask communications are given in the software framework. Moreover, the flight control software is designed as an example under this framework after a brief introduction of the flight control system and the software design requirement for stratospheric aerostat. To make sure that the software design methodology is feasible in the system of stratospheric aerostat, the schedulability analysis is implemented using the rate monotonic (RM) scheduling algorithm.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Since stratospheric aerostat has the overwhelming superiority in long time stay, strong viability and big payload capacity, it becomes a new flight platform that many countries are competing to develop. There are some related projects such as "High-Altitude Airship" (HAA) of Lockheed Martin Company of the United States, "Hisentinel" airship [2] of Southwest Research Institute of the United States, "Satellites" of Sanswire Company, high-altitude research platform [3] of NASA, "Stratospheric Airship Program" [4] of South Korea, etc. Besides, it can be applied to various platforms such as communication, surveillance, electronic warfare and technology demonstration, etc.

Because of the design constraints of high flight altitude and long time stay, the above stratosphere aerostat projects are generally designed for unmanned platforms. And all the functions of flight control, parameter measurement and system management are implemented by airborne computer software. Therefore, the reliability and real-time reaction ability of the software plays an important role in the system of stratospheric aerostat. As typical embedded software, it has two kinds of designing methods according to the existence of operating system. In our project, the software is designed based on the VxWorks embedded real-time operating system with masses of equipment management, complex data processing and high reliability requirement taken into account.

Since VxWorks possesses friendly development environment, high-performance kernel, good real-time capability, stability and reliability, it has been widely used in satellites, communications, military, aviation, aerospace and other high-tech fields. Here we will not go further on the related introduction about VxWorks. For the details, please refer to [1]. In this paper, a brief introduction of the flight control system and the software design requirement for stratospheric aerostat are given first. After that, we present a kind of general application software framework for unmanned air vehicle (UAV) airborne computer based on the VxWorks operating system. Furthermore, the flight control software is designed as an example under this framework. At last, we implement the schedulability analysis using the rate monotonic (RM) scheduling algorithm to make sure that the software design methodology is feasible in the system of stratospheric aerostat.

div.head: II. BRIEF INTRODUCTION OF FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM
div.p: The avionic system of stratospheric aerostat consists of flight control system and management system. The flight control system primarily achieves the goal of autonomous taking off, cruising and landing by computing the control laws, while the management system mainly carries out the functions of remote control and telemetry, energy management, data collection, payload management, etc.
In our project, the following subsystems and equipment are contained in flight control system, and the frame of flight control system is shown in Fig. 1.

div.head: 1) Dual Redundant Flight Control Computers
div.p: The dual redundant flight control compute is the central part of the flight control system. It implements autonomous control of the stratospheric aerostat by exchanging data with devices.

div.head: 2) Integrated Navigation System
div.p: The integrated navigation system is used to measure the navigation data of stratospheric aerostat real-timely, such as position, angle, speed, angular rate, etc.

div.head: 3) Propulsion System
div.p: As the main executing system, the propulsion system is controlled by the flight control computers to achieve the autonomous cruising and stay.

div.head: 4) Valve Control System
div.p: The valve control system is used to carry out altitude control of the aerostat by computing the control laws for taking off and landing.

div.head: 5) Airspeed Transducer Syetem
div.p: The airspeed is measured by the airspeed transducer system real-timely. Moreover, it can be used to compute the angle of attack and sideslip by combining with the navigation data.

div.head: 6) Emergency Parachute System
div.p: The emergency parachute system is used to save the expensive avionics when unexpected emergency occurs.

div.head: 7) Landing Deceleration Aid System
div.p: The landing deceleration aid system is used to reduce the vertical velocity while landing.

div.head: 8) Barometric Altimeter, Radio Altimeter
div.p: The barometric altitude is used to adjust the navigation data. While landing, the radio altitude is used for reference. Considering the huge size of the stratospheric aerostat, CAN bus is used to complete data exchanges between devices, meanwhile 1553B bus to transmit abundant remote control and telemetry data. Besides, in order to realize the redundancy management, these two flight control computers communicate with each other through cross communication data link (CCDL).

div.head: III. FLIGHT CONTROL SOFTWARE DESIGN REQUIREMENT
div.p: According to Fig. 1, as well as some analysis on the system design requirements, the following functions must be fulfilled by the flight control software.

div.head: 1) Flight Control Law Computation
div.p: The control laws can be computed periodically by this software in the autonomous flight mode, which mainly contains control laws for taking off, cruising, stay and landing. By CAN bus, the computation result is transmitted to the propulsion system, the valve control system, the landing deceleration aid system and the emergency parachute system.

div.head: 2) Redundancy Management
div.p: The dual redundant flight control computers crosscompare the result computed by CCDL to ensure that there is only one output channel for each period.

div.head: 3) Navigation Data Processing
div.p: As the navigation data read from the integrated navigation system cannot be used to compute control laws directly, it needs to be transformed to useful data. In the software, the useful navigation data is worked out by combining with the data of integrated navigation system, airspeed transducer system and barometric altimeter.

div.head: 4) Routes Importing
div.p: The routes and stay parameters can be imported to the control computers before taking off as well as while flying.

div.head: 5) Data Exchanging Between Devices
div.p: The software can input and output data with other devices.

div.head: 6) Test
div.p: Test is used to detect faults of computers, subsystems and devices.

div.head: 7) Fault Management
div.p: The software is capable of recording and dealing with faults while flying.

div.head: IV. GENERAL SOFTWARE FRAMWORK DESIGN
div.p: According to the above functions, airborne computer software consists of system software and application software. System software plays a role of supportting programs like interface drivers and task scheduling procedures. On the other side, application software is a concentrated expression of the system functionality. The software framework and flight control software designed in this paper belong to the application software, and the system software is implemented by the VxWorks operating system. This section will design a general software framework for UAV based on VxWorks.

Task design is the most important part in designing embedded application software for a specific UAV. The designing of task classification, priorities and intertask communications will affect the quality of the software directly. Therefore, we will focus our attention on the task design methodology in the following software framework.

div.head: A. Software Structure Design
div.p: The application software is divided into different tasks. When the system is started, the initialization module begins to run firstly and all the global data and tasks are initialized. Then each task is running under the scheduling of VxWorks. The running structure of the application software is shown in Fig. 2.

div.head: B. Task Design 1) Task Classification
div.p: According to the operation mode of tasks, three types of tasks are designed in the framework.

div.head: a) Time-driven Task
div.p: The task activated by clock interrupt service routine (ISR) is called time-driven task. Periodic task is a typical timedriven task. It is used to fulfill the functions which must be executed periodically. The number of periodic tasks may be more than one and they may have different running periods. Therefore, in the specific software, the greatest common divisor of running periods of all the periodic tasks can be set to the period of clock interrupts. And the clock ISR is capable of sending different binary semaphores to activate the relevant periodic task.

div.head: b) Event-driven Task
div.p: The task activated by random events is called eventdriven task. The typical event-driven tasks include input task, output task and fault management task. The data read from equipment is managed by input task. Output task is used to output data to the different devices and the fault management task is used to record and deal with faults. The event-driven tasks are pended at peacetime, they shall not turn into ready or running state until the required resource is ready.

To enhance the portability of software, the standard data structure should be designed for different kinds of interfaces. So the data of devices must be transformed into standard structure before being managed by input task. Meanwhile the data must be specified before being outputted to specific devices.

c) Background Running Task Some functions have no strict real-time requirements, so they can be executed in background while other tasks are delayed or pended. For example, test task is a kind of background running task. The test task will send message to the fault management task if the fault is detected.

div.head: 2) Task Priorities
div.p: As event-driven tasks must manage random events instantly, they are allocated the highest priorities. Background running task has the lowest priority, since the real-time capability is not required in this kind of task.

In the event-driven tasks, fault management task has the highest priority because it must deal with faults in time, and input task takes the second place while output task is the lowest. The design for priorities of all the tasks is shown in Fig. 3.

div.head: C. Other Programs
div.p: In addition to the above mentioned tasks, the software has some other programs need to be run.

div.head: 1) System Initialization program
div.p: The system initialization program takes charge of the initialization of global data, interfaces of devices, tasks, etc.

div.head: 2) Clock ISR
div.p: The clock ISR is capable of sending different binary semaphores to activate the relevant periodic task.

div.head: 3) Input ISR
div.p: The input ISR serves input and standardization work firstly, and then sends the data of standard structure to input task to manage.

div.head: 4) Output Interface Program
div.p: Output interface program is mainly to achieve the specification and output work.

div.head: D. Intertask communications Design
div.p: Intertask communications permit independent tasks to coordinate their actions, and VxWorks supplies a rich set of intertask communication mechanisms, such as shared memory, semaphores, message queues, pipes, signals, etc.

For input task and output task, message queues is used to communicate with other tasks of the software framework, and periodic task takes shared memory. All the tasks will send messages to fault management task while the fault is detected. The global data is protected by mutual-exclusion semaphores. The design of the tasks and the intertask communications are shown in Fig. 4. According to the design requirements, the flight control software for stratospheric aerostat is designed by combining with the software framework.

div.head: 1) Time-driven Task Design
div.p: In the flight control software, the periodic tasks consist of collection periodic task and control periodic task. The period of collection periodic task is 0.1s, and the collection periodic task is used to read the radio altitude from radio altimeter. Meanwhile, the control periodic task runs one time per 0.02s. Control periodic task is used to fulfill four functions, which are redundancy management, processing of navigation data, processing of routes data and computing of control laws.

The period of clock interrupts is set to 0.02s. A binary semaphore is given to the control periodic task in the clock ISR for each period and another one is given to the collection periodic task every ten periods in the same way.

div.head: 2) Event-driven Task Design
div.p: In the flight control software, the input tasks consist of CAN input task, 1553B input task and RS422 input task. The CAN input task takes charge of managing standard CAN data which is received from the message queues, and the 1553B input task is responsible for standard 1553B data as well. The RS422 input task is designed to read the barometric altitude from barometric altimeter. The standard CAN and 1553B data are generated from related input ISR.
The output task of flight control software is used to output CAN data and 1553B data.
The fault management task can record and deal with the faults.

div.head: 3) Background Running Task Design
div.p: The test task of flight control software adopts the same functions as the test task of the framework.

The task classification of flight control software has been described above, and other designs can refer to the software framework like task priorities and intertask communications. The task designing of flight control software for stratospheric aerostat is shown in Fig. 5.

div.head: B. Schedulability Analysis
div.p: In order to make sure that all the designed tasks can be scheduled correctly, task schedulability analysis must be implemented. For real-time systems, the analytical method used commonly is RM scheduling algorithm [6]. Based on some assumptions, Liu and Layland presented a RM algorithm to determine the schedulability condition by the utilization of CPU, which is outlined as follows.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION
div.p: Although the flight control software for stratospheric aerostat is chosen as the designing background, a general software framework based on the VxWorks operating system is put forward for UAV application software designing. Using this framework, detailed designing can be carried by combining with specific requirements. In addition, the validity and reliability of this framework has been verified and tested on the prototype aerostat system.
